record.original_question: For the three-dimensional Brezis-Nirenberg Dirichlet problem -Delta u = lambda u + |u|^(2*-2)u in a general bounded domain Omega subset of R^3, with u = 0 on partial Omega and, if needed, Omega assumed convex, are there infinitely many sign-changing solutions of arbitrarily large energy for every lambda > 0?

evidence.quote: In [57], it was proved that (1.1) in the unit ball Omega = B(0, 1) has infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions with arbitrary large energy for every lambda > 0.
When the domain is a three-dimensional cuboid (rectangular prism), Sun, Wei, and Yang [58] proved the existence of infinitely many sign-changing solutions.
Open question 2: In a general bounded domain Omega, if necessary, it could be convex, are there infinitely many sign-changing solutions of (1.1) with arbitrary large energy for any lambda > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain (which may be assumed convex if necessary), and let $2^* = 6$ denote the critical Sobolev exponent in dimension three. Consider the Brezis–Nirenberg problem
$$
\begin{cases}
-\Delta u = \lambda u + |u|^{2^*-2} u & \text{in } \Omega, \\
u = 0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega.
\end{cases}
$$
A weak solution $u \in H_0^1(\Omega)$ is called sign-changing if both $u^+ = \max(u,0)$ and $u^- = \max(-u,0)$ are nontrivial. The energy of a solution is
$$
E(u) = \frac{1}{2}\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^2 \, dx - \frac{\lambda}{2}\int_\Omega u^2\, dx - \frac{1}{2^*}\int_\Omega |u|^{2^*}\, dx.
$$
Prove or disprove: for every $\lambda > 0$, the problem above admits infinitely many sign-changing solutions whose energies are unbounded above.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is known for special domains in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the unit ball admits infinitely many non-radial sign-changing solutions of arbitrarily large energy for every $\lambda > 0$, and for cuboids infinitely many sign-changing solutions are also known. For a general (or even general convex) bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, no such result has been established; the question remains stated as an open problem in current literature.

status_evidence.title: Infinitely many sign-changing solutions for the Brézis-Nirenberg problem
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for infinitely many sign-changing solutions are known in dimensions N ≥ 7, with the 3D case posing additional challenges.
status_evidence.claim: The general 3D case is recognized as substantially harder than higher dimensions and not resolved for general bounded domains.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
status_evidence.snippet: Recent progress includes infinitely many sign-changing nonradial solutions in symmetric/special domains using Yamabe-type building blocks.
status_evidence.claim: Available 3D results rely on special geometry (ball, cuboid, star-shaped); a general-domain answer is not provided.
